title: Joint path and reciprocal gain constraints kept the 1.608 correction factor in one selected worm response sample
abstract: We tested a joint correction of selected C. elegans calcium response means against necessary steady passive conditions. One common factor of 1.607704 met all 1,171 covered path bounds, 82 pair bounds and 82 reciprocal gain constraints in the primary sample. This equals the prior single-path lower bound. Shared entries added no requirement. In the subset with at least 10 occurrences, reciprocal gain constraints raised the minimum from 1.402870 to 1.506473. A four-edge cycle gave a matching lower bound. Primal and dual audits, direct feasibility brackets and a synthetic cycle check passed. These are model consistency results, not measured error estimates or evidence against passive physiology. Finite calcium windows can violate the steady bounds in passive circuits. Pooled data, selection, uncertain gains and absent matched animals limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact source hashes and external regeneration steps are supplied. Source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Common correction factors for overlapping selected response samples. The primary joint factor equals the largest separate-path factor. Reciprocal gain constraints add a requirement only in the occurrence-10 subset.

citations.reason: Joint correction extends the prior path test; no source code or tables reused.
